859.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace. Raag Gond, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). If you keep your hope in the Lord, in your mind and heart, you will gain many, many fruits your mind desires; the Lord knows all that passes within the soul; God lets not even a sesame seed's worth of anyone's labour go to waste. O my mind, hope should be placed in that Lord, the Master who pervades all. O my mind, set your hope on the Lord of the world, the earth's Master. Any hope that is placed in anyone but the Lord is fruitless; that hope all goes in vain. All the family you see is attachment to Maya (the world's illusion and lure); beware of wasting your life clinging to hope in it. Nothing is in their hands; what can these poor ones do? Their striving avails nothing. O my mind, place your hope in the Lord, your own Beloved, who carries you across and sets all your family free. If you place any other hope, in Maya, do not imagine it will be of any use to you. This hope in Maya is the love of another; it is false, and in an instant it all perishes. O my mind, place your hope in the Lord, your true Beloved, who accepts all your labour. All hope and desire are yours, my Master; as you make one hope, so does one hope. Nothing is in anyone's hands, my Master; such is the understanding my True Guru has given me. You know servant Nanak's hope; beholding the Lord's sight, he is fulfilled by the Lord's sight. ॥4॥
Chaupade (chau, four; pad, stanza): hymns of four stanzas.
860.1: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). One should serve such a Lord, and meditate on him every day, who destroys all sins in an instant. If one forsakes the Lord and places hope in another, the Lord makes all one's labour fruitless and lets it go to waste. O my mind, serve the Lord, the Master, the giver of peace; serving him, all hunger departs. O my mind, one should put one's trust in the Lord. Wherever one goes, my Master is there alongside; the Lord keeps the honour of his servants and slaves as his own. If you tell your pain to others, they in return lay out their own pain, ever so much more. Tell your pain to the Lord, your own Master, who cuts away your sorrows at once. Should one leave such a God and tell one's pain to others? Telling it to others, O mind, one dies of shame. The family, friends and brothers of the world whom you see, O my mind, all meet (you) for their own ends. On the day their purpose is not served, on that day not one comes near. O my mind, serve your own Lord day and night, who helps you in sorrow and in joy. Why should one trust, O my mind, one who cannot save (us) at the final hour? Take the Guru's teaching and repeat the mantra of the Lord's Name; those with the Lord's love in their hearts are set free by him at the end. Says servant Nanak, O Sants (saints) of the Lord, repeat the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) night and day; this is the true assurance of release. ॥4॥
860.2: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). Remembering the Lord, there is bliss and peace always, calm within, and one's own mind grows cool, as when the sun of Maya blazes fiercely, and on seeing the Guru, the moon, all the burning passes away. O my mind, night and day meditate on the Naam and repeat (the Name of) the Lord. He protects you wherever you are, in every place; serve such a God, your own, for ever. O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, in whom are all treasures; through the Guru, search and find the jewel of the Lord. Those who meditated on the Lord found the Lord, my Master; massage the feet of those servants of the Lord. Recognise the Shabad (the Word) and receive the essence of Ram (the Lord); (one who does) becomes an exalted Sant, the greatest of the great. The Lord himself has increased the glory of that servant; he is not lessened by anyone's lessening, not by a sesame seed, not by the least bit. O my mind, the One from whom you receive comforts, meditate on him always, ever with joined palms. O Lord, give servant Nanak one gift: may your feet, Lord, dwell ever in my heart. ॥4॥
861.1: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). All the rich, the emperors, the nobles, the chiefs and the headmen there are, are perishable; know that the love of another is false. The Lord is imperishable, ever abiding, unmoving; worship him, O my mind, and you will be accepted. O my mind, worship the Name of the Lord, (your) everlasting support. One who attains the Lord's mansion through the Guru's words: no one else has strength as great as his. All the wealthy, the high-born and the owners of land that you see, O my mind, will perish like the fleeting colour of the safflower. O my mind, ever serve the Lord, the True One, the Niranjan (the One untouched by Maya), through whom you will win honour in the Lord's court. Brahmin, Khatri, Shudra and Vaish: there are four varnas (castes) and four ashrams; whoever meditates on the Lord is foremost. As the lowly castor plant dwells beside the sandalwood (and takes its fragrance), so joining the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), the fallen one is accepted. Highest of all and purest of all is the one in whose heart God has come to dwell. Servant Nanak washes the feet of that servant of the Lord who serves him, though he be of low caste. ॥4॥
Kasumbh, the safflower, gives a bright dye that soon fades.

The four ashrams: in Hindu custom the four stages of life, the student (brahmacharya), the householder (grihasth), the forest-dweller (vanaprasth) and the renunciant (sannyas), each with its own duties.
861.2: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). The Lord is the Knower of hearts, at work in all; as the Lord makes one act, so one acts. Serve such a Lord always, O my mind, who saves you from everything. O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord; the Lord should be recited every day. No one but the Lord can kill or bring to life; then, O my mind, why should one fret? The Lord, the Creator, has made this whole expanse, and has himself placed his own light within it. The one Lord speaks, the one Lord makes (all) speak; the perfect Guru has made (me) see the one Lord. The Lord is with (us) within and with (us) without; say, O mind, what should one hide from him? One should serve the Lord without guile; then, O my mind, every comfort is gained. The One in whose power is everything is the greatest of all; O my mind, he should be meditated on always. O servant Nanak, that Lord is with you; meditate on the Lord always, and he will set you free. ॥4॥
861.3: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji). My mind burns greatly for the sight of the Lord, like one who thirsts without water. The love of the Lord has pierced my mind like an arrow. The Lord God knows my suffering, the ache within my mind. Whoever tells me any word of my Beloved Lord is my brother, my own dear brother. Meet me, meet me, my friend, and tell (me) the virtues of my God, taking the steadying counsel of the True Guru. O Lord, fulfil servant Nanak's hope; in the Lord's sight the body finds peace.
Chhaka 1: the first set of six shabads; the count is written after the shabad's numbers.
862.1: Raag Gond, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. (God) is the doer of all, and the enjoyer of all. It is the Creator who hears, the Creator who sees; the unseen is the Creator, the seen is the Creator; the Creator brings creation, the Creator brings dissolution; the Creator pervades all, and the Creator stays untouched. It is the Creator who speaks, the Creator who understands; the Creator comes, and the Creator too goes; the Creator is Nirgun, the Creator is Sargun; O Nanak, by the Guru's grace (one gains) the eye that sees (him) alike in all. ॥2॥
Nirgun: God beyond the three qualities of Maya; Sargun: God made manifest in the creation, with its qualities.
862.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Like the fish and the monkey, you are caught and tangled up in the safflower (of fleeting Maya). Every step you take and every breath you draw is counted; sing the Lord's praises, and only then will you be saved. O mind, understand, and give up your waywardness. You find no place (here) to dwell for yourself; why then do you go to another's (house)? As the elephant is driven by the lure of lust, so you cling to your family. As birds gather and then part again, (so is the family); become steady in the Sangat and meditate on the Lord, Har Har. As the fish perishes through the taste of the tongue, so the fool, lured by greed, is robbed; you have fallen into the power of the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride); fall at (the Lord's) refuge, and only so will you be freed. Be merciful, O destroyer of the sorrows of the meek; all beings and creatures are yours. May I receive this gift, to behold your sight for ever; come and meet Nanak, the servant of your servants. ॥4॥

A monkey is trapped with grain put in a narrow-mouthed pot: the full fist will not come out, and the greedy monkey will not let go, so he is caught. The fish dies through taste, on the bait. The elephant is said to be caught by a paper she-elephant set over a covered pit.
862.3: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. The One who fashioned (you) and gave (you) soul and breath, who in his kindness placed (his) light in the clay (of the body), (who gave you) everything to use, and (who) feeds you foods to enjoy: forsaking that God, O fool, where do you go? Let me devote myself to the service of the Supreme Lord. It is through the Guru that the Niranjan, the divine Lord, is known. The One who has made colours of many kinds, (who brings about) creation and dissolution in the twinkling of an eye, whose state and extent cannot be told: O my mind, meditate on that God for ever. The Master neither comes nor goes; he is unmoving. His virtues are endless; how many can I count? The One whose storehouses are full of the rubies of the Name gives support to every heart. The One whose Name is Sat Purakh (the True Being who pervades all): millions of sins are erased: sing his praise for even an instant. He is the companion from childhood, the friend of the devotees, the support of the breath of life, the love of Nanak's heart. ॥4॥
863.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I have done my trading with the Naam; the Naam alone is the support of this mind; in my heart I have taken the Naam alone as my shelter; repeating the Naam, millions of sins are erased. As (my) capital, the Lord has given (me) the one Naam; (the Naam) is my mind's beloved object of worship; in the Guru's company (my) attention dwells (on it). The Naam is the capital of my soul; wherever I go, the Naam alone is my companion; the Naam alone has become sweet to my mind; in water, on land, in all, I have seen the Naam alone. Through the Naam, faces are radiant in the Lord's court; through the Naam, all one's generations have been saved; by the Naam my affairs have been accomplished; this mind has grown fond of the Naam. Through the Naam alone I have grown fearless; through the Naam, (my) coming and going (in births) has ended; the perfect Guru has brought (me) to the Treasure of virtues. Says Nanak, (my) dwelling is (now) in peace and in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise). ॥4॥
863.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The One who gives honour to the dishonoured, who gives his gifts to all the hungry, who protects (us) in the dreadful womb: to that Master be salutation for ever. Meditate in your mind on such a God, the helper in easy places and in hard, wherever one may be. To whom the pauper and the king are alike, who fills all, the worm and the elephant, who asks no second one and takes no one's counsel: whatever he does, he does himself. Whose end no one can know: he, the Niranjan, is all himself; he himself is form, he himself is formless; (he dwells) in every heart, the support of all hearts. In the dye of the Naam, the devotees have become deep red; singing (his) praise, the Sants are ever in delight; in the love of the Naam, (his) servants remain fulfilled; Nanak falls at the feet of those servants. ॥4॥
863.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Those in whose company this mind (becomes) pure, in whose company there is Simran (remembrance) of the Lord, Har Har, in whose company sins are destroyed, in whose company the heart is filled with light: those Sants of the Lord are my friends, in whose presence the Naam alone is sung every day. By whose mantra the Lord, Har Har, comes to dwell in the mind, by whose teaching doubt and fear flee, in whose presence is (the Lord's) pure and sublime praise, whose dust (of the feet) the world longs for; in whose company millions of the fallen are saved, whose support is the Name of the one Formless Lord, (who) knows the hidden heart of every being, the treasure of mercy, the Niranjan, the divine Lord. When the Supreme Lord became merciful, then (I) met the Guru, the merciful Saadh (the holy one). Nanak meditates on the Naam day and night; through the Lord's Name come peace, Sahaj and bliss. ॥4॥
864.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In my mind I meditate on the form of the Guru; through the Guru's Shabad, my mind holds to the mantra (of the Name); I take the Guru's feet and enshrine them in my heart; to the Guru, the Supreme Lord, I bow for ever. Let no one in the world be misled by doubt: without the Guru no one will cross over. The Guru has set the strayed upon the path; having (him) give up all else, he has joined him to the Lord's devotion; he has erased the dread of birth and death. Boundless is the greatness of the perfect Guru. By the Guru's grace, the inverted lotus (of the heart) blossoms; in the darkness, light has dawned; the One who made (us) has been known through the Guru; by the Guru's grace the foolish mind has been won over. The Guru is the Creator; the Guru has power to do all; the Guru is the Supreme God, who is and also shall be. Says Nanak, God has made this known (to me): without the Guru, O brother, liberation is not attained. ॥4॥
The inverted lotus: the heart turned away from God, like a lotus hanging upside down and closed; turned towards him, it opens as the lotus does.
864.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Say Guru, Guru, Guru, O my mind. Without the Guru I have no other. Stay in the Guru's support day and night, whose gift no one can erase. Know the Guru and the Supreme God as one; what pleases him is accepted. The one whose mind is fixed on the Guru's feet: his sorrow, pain and doubt run away. Serving the Guru, one gains honour; (I am) ever a sacrifice to the Guru. Beholding the Guru's sight, (the mind) is filled with delight; the labour of the Guru's servant comes to fruition; no sorrow afflicts the Guru's servant; the Guru's servant is known in all ten directions. The Guru's greatness is beyond telling; the Guru, the Supreme Lord, pervades (all). Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is perfect has his mind fixed on the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
864.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Guru is my worship; the Guru is Gobind (the Lord of the universe); my Guru is Paarbrahm (the Supreme Lord); the Guru is God; my Guru is the divine Lord, unseen and beyond knowing; I serve the Guru's feet, which all worship. Without the Guru there is no other place for me; night and day I repeat the name of the Guru, the Guru. The Guru is my wisdom; the Guru is the meditation in my heart; the Guru is Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), the all-pervading Being, God; with joined palms I remain in the Guru's refuge; without the Guru I have no other. The Guru is the ship that carries (us) across the ocean of the world; through the Guru's service comes release from Jam (the messenger of Death); the Guru's mantra is light amid the darkness; in the Guru's company, all are delivered. It is by great good fortune that the perfect Guru is found; serving the Guru, sorrow does not touch (one); no one can erase the Guru's Shabad; the Guru is Nanak, and Nanak is that Lord himself. ॥4॥
865.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Do your trading with (the Name of) Ram, Ram; (make) Ram, Ram, Ram the support of your breath of life; sing the Kirtan (songs of God's praise) of Ram, Ram, Ram; the all-pervading Ram is contained in all. Join the Sants and utter (the Name of) Ram: (this) is the purest of all deeds, one that is complete. Gather the wealth of Ram, Ram, and fill (your) storehouse; make Ram, Ram, Ram your food; may (the Name of) Ram, Ram never be forgotten: the Guru, in his mercy, has told (me this). Ram, Ram, Ram is ever the helper; fix your attention in love on Ram, Ram, Ram; repeating Ram, Ram, (they) have become pure, and the sins of birth after birth have gone. Remembering Ram, (he) ends birth and death; uttering Ram, (he) carries (one) across (the ocean of) fear. Ram, the radiant One, is highest of all; O servant Nanak, repeat (his Name) night and day. ॥4॥
865.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Master held them (the five) in check, and they were beaten; he beat them and drove them away from (his) servant. They could not find the mansion of Gobind's devotee; the servants of Ram have joined together and sung songs of joy. The five chiefs of all creation (the five enemies) are water-carriers to the devotee of Ram. They take tribute from the world, but bow in salute to Gobind's devotee; they plunder the Saakats (those who have turned from God) and strip them of honour, but they rub and wash the feet of the holy. One mother (Maya) has borne five sons; making the play of the earth-born (and the other sources of life), she has given birth to the world. (Beings) revel, absorbed in the three qualities (of Maya); leaving these behind, (the Lord's) servants dwell above. In his mercy (the Lord) has set his servants free; the One whose (servants) they are has kept (the five) away from them. Says Nanak, devotion to God is the essence; without devotion, all are ruined. ॥4॥
The four sources of life (khaani): birth from the egg, from the womb, from sweat and from the earth.
The three qualities (gunas) of Maya: rajas, sattva and tamas, under which all deeds are done.
865.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Through the Lord's Name, strife and anguish have been erased; sorrows have been destroyed, and peace has made its home (within); repeating again and again the Naam, the Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life), (his servants) are fulfilled; by the Sant's grace (they) have obtained every fruit. Repeating Ram, (his) servants have crossed over; the sins of birth after birth have been taken away. Those who have enshrined the Guru's feet in the heart, within the breast, have crossed over the ocean of fire; all the torment of birth and death is erased; in Sahaj, (they) are absorbed in God. In every place and space is the one Master; he is the Knower of all hearts; the one to whom, in his mercy, he gives understanding takes God's Name at all hours. The one within whom God himself dwells: in his heart there is light. With loving devotion, one should sing the Lord's Kirtan; O Nanak, repeating (the Name of) the Supreme Lord, one is carried across. ॥4॥
865.4: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Bow to the lotus feet of the Guru; slay lust and anger, (driving them) out of this body; one should live as the dust (of the feet) of all; recognise the all-pervading Lord in every heart, in all. In this way remember Gopal, Gobind: the body and wealth are God's, and the soul is God's. Sing the Lord's praises at all hours; this is the purpose of soul and breath; give up pride and know God to be with (you); by the Saadh's grace, dye your mind in the Lord('s love). Know the One who made you; (such a one) wins honour hereafter in the Lord's court; (his) mind and body become pure and filled with delight, as the tongue repeats the Name of Gopal. Show mercy, my (Lord), merciful to the meek: (my) mind asks for the dust under the Saadh's feet. Be kind, O God, and give (this) gift: that Nanak may live by repeating God's Name. ॥4॥
866.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Service of Gopal is (my) incense and lamp; to the Creator (I) bow countless times. Leaving all else, (I) have taken hold of God's refuge; by great good fortune, the Guru is greatly pleased (with me). At all hours one should sing of Gobind; the body and wealth are God's, and the soul is God's. Uttering the Lord's virtues, joy has come; the Supreme Lord is all-pervading, the one who forgives. In his mercy he joins his servants to his service, erases (their) pain of birth and death, and unites (them with himself). This is the (true) deed, this the dharma, this the essence of wisdom: in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) one should repeat the Lord's Name. Cross the (world-)ocean on the ship of the feet of God, who knows every heart and does and causes all to be done. Bestowing his mercy, (God) has kept (his own) safe; the five dreadful enemies have fled. (The Lord's servant) never loses (his) life in the gamble; the Creator has taken Nanak's side. ॥4॥
866.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). In his mercy (God) grants peace and bliss; the divine Guru has kept (his) children safe. God, Gobind, is kind and merciful, the forgiver of all beings and creatures. (I have come to) your refuge, God, merciful to the meek; repeating (the Name of) the Supreme Lord, one is ever in delight. O God, there is none other so merciful; you are within every heart, contained in all. (God) sets right this world and the next for his servant; to purify the fallen, O God, is your age-old way. Remember Gobind: (this is) millions of medicines; one should worship the Lord: (this is) the tantra and the mantra. Meditating on God, illness and grief are wiped away, and one gains in full the fruits the mind desires. (God) does and causes all to be done; he is all-powerful and merciful; in deep reflection on him lie all treasures. O Nanak, God himself has forgiven (his servants); for ever and ever repeat (the Name of) the one Lord. ॥4॥
866.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, my friend; your mind will become pure. Every affliction of mind and body is erased, and all pain and darkness depart. Singing the Lord's praises, one crosses the world (-ocean); by great good fortune, the infinite Being is found. The one who sings the Kirtan of Gopal cannot be touched by Jamkaal (death). His coming into the world is approved; through the Guru, recognise your own Master. (The one who) sings the Lord's praises by the Sant's grace: (his) frenzies of lust and anger are erased. Know the Lord to be ever present; (this is) the perfect Guru's flawless mantra. (One who) has earned the wealth of the Lord and filled (his) storehouses has, meeting the True Guru, set all (his) affairs right; (he) has woken up, dyed in the Lord's Name; O Nanak, (his) mind clings to the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
867.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The Lord's feet are the ship across the world-ocean; remembering the Naam, there is no dying again. Uttering the Lord's praises, one does not walk the road of Jam; deep reflection (on God) crushes the five enemies. I have come to your refuge, O perfect Master; give your hand to your own creature. The Simritis, the Shastras, the Vedas and the Puranas expound the Supreme Lord; yogis, celibates, Vaishnavs and servants of Ram (tell of him too), (yet) God, the Imperishable, has no measure. Shiva and the gods cry out in entreaty, (but) they grasp not a sesame seed's worth of the unseen, unfathomable (Lord). Whoever is given loving devotion by (God) himself: such are rare in the world, only one here and there. In me, who am without virtue, there is no virtue at all; in your glance (of grace) are all the treasures. Nanak, the meek, begs for your service; be merciful, O divine Guru, and grant (it). ॥4॥
867.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). (God says:) the one cursed by the Sant I tear out from the earth; the Sant's slanderer I hurl down from the sky. The Sant I keep close to my own soul; the Sant I save at once, in the time of a hand-clap. He alone is a Sant who is pleasing to Ram; the Sant and Gobind have but one work. God places (his) hand over the Sant, and dwells with the Sant day and night. Breath by breath he sustains the Sants; the Sant's foe he casts down from (his) throne. Let no one slander the Sant; whoever slanders comes to ruin. The one whom the Creator protects: let the whole world strive in vain (against him). Trust in one's own God has come; soul and body are all his capital. This conviction has arisen in Nanak: the manmukh (the self-willed) loses, and the Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) ever wins. ॥4॥
867.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Water (your heart) with the immaculate Name of Narayan; remembering it with the tongue, sins melt away. Narayan dwells in all; Narayan shines forth in every heart. Those who utter (the Name of) Narayan do not go to hell; serving Narayan, they obtain all fruits. Narayan is the support within the mind; Narayan is the ship across the world (-ocean). Uttering (the Name of) Narayan, Jam turns and flees; Narayan has broken the teeth of the witch (Maya). Narayan is for ever and ever the forgiver; Narayan has brought peace and bliss; Narayan has made (his) glory manifest; Narayan is the mother and father of the Sant. In the Saadh Sangat it is Narayan, Narayan; again and again Narayan is sung. Meeting the Guru, (I) have found the thing beyond the reach of the senses; servant Nanak has taken hold of Narayan's shelter. ॥4॥
868.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). The one whom the Protector protects: the Formless Lord takes his side. In the mother's womb, fire does not afflict him; lust, anger, greed and attachment cannot touch him; in the Saadh Sangat he repeats (the Name of) the Formless Lord; ashes fall on the face of (his) slanderer. (The Name of) Ram is the servant's shield and coat of mail; the wicked foes cannot touch him. Whoever takes pride (in himself) is undone; the humble servant's refuge is God (himself). Whoever has entered the refuge of the Lord, the King: that servant (God) has kept safe, clasped to his bosom. If anyone is very proud, in an instant he is mingled with the dust. The True One is now, and shall ever be; I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever. Showing mercy, he has kept his servants safe; Nanak's God is the support of the breath of life. ॥4॥
868.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Wondrous is the account, utterly beyond compare: the soul is the form of the Supreme Lord. It is neither old nor a child; it has no pain, nor the net of Jam; it neither perishes nor is born; from the beginning, from the start of the ages, it has pervaded (all). It feels no heat, it feels no cold; it has no enemy, it has no friend; it knows no elation, it knows no grief; all things are its own; it has the power to do (all). It has no father, it has no mother; it lies past the farthest beyond, and has existed from the first. The stain of sin and of virtue does not cling to it; within every heart it is ever awake. (God) created the one Shakti (Maya), with its three qualities; this great Maya is his shadow. He cannot be deceived or pierced, his secret cannot be known; he is merciful, merciful to the meek, ever kind. Of his state and extent nothing at all can be found; Nanak goes as a sacrifice to him, again and again. ॥4॥
869.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). I am a sacrifice to the Sants; in the company of the Sants (I) sing the praises of Ram. By the Sants' grace all sins are gone; those of great fortune enter the Sants' refuge. Repeating (the Name of) Ram, no obstacle takes hold; by the Guru's grace one's own God is made known. When the Supreme Lord becomes merciful, he turns (one) into dust at the feet of the holy; lust and anger leave this body, and the jewel of Ram comes to dwell in the mind. Fruitful and approved is the birth of that one (who knows God to be near): know the Supreme Lord to be near at hand. With loving devotion he is absorbed in God's Kirtan, and, asleep for birth after birth, he awakens. (God's) lotus feet are his servant's support; I utter the praises of Govind: (this is) the true trade. (O God,) fulfil the longing of (your) servants: may Nanak find peace in the dust of (your) servants. ॥4॥
869.2: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji). Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Bow to the perfect divine Guru, whose very form bears fruit, whose service bears fruit; (he is) the knower of hearts, the all-pervading Being, the Creator; at all hours (he is) dyed in the love of the Naam. The Guru is Gobind, the Guru is Gopal, the protector of his own servant. (The Guru) has won over emperors, kings and nobles; he has struck down and destroyed the wicked and the proud; he has put disease into the slanderer's mouth; all the world hails (his) victory. In the minds of the Sants is great bliss; the Sants repeat (the Name of) the divine Guru, the Lord. The faces of the Sangat have grown radiant; the slanderer has lost every place (to stand). With every breath the servant ever praises the Supreme Lord, the Guru free of all want, in whose refuge all fears are erased; (he) has struck all slanderers down to the ground. Let no one slander the servant (of the Lord); whoever does comes to grief. At all hours the servant meditates on the One; Jam does not go near him. The servants are without enmity, the slanderers are proud; the servants wish (all) well, the slanderers are given to vice. The Guru's Sikh has meditated on the True Guru; the servants are saved; the slanderer has been cast into hell. Listen, my friend, my dear companion: at the Lord's door true words hold good: as one does, so one receives; the proud one's root is surely torn out. O True Guru, the unsupported have you alone to lean on; be merciful and keep (the honour) of your servant. Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru, remembering whom (my) honour has been upheld. ॥8॥
870.1: Raag Gond, the hymns of the Bhagats: Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. When one meets a Sant, one should listen a little and speak a little; when one meets one who is no Sant, one should keep silent. O Baba, what kind of speech should one speak, by which one may stay absorbed in the Name of Ram? Speaking with the Sants does good; speaking with a fool is labour in vain. Talking on and on, the vices grow; (yet) without speaking, what reflection can (people) make? Says Kabir: the empty pitcher makes a sound; the one that is full never wavers. ॥4॥
870.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. When a man dies, the man serves no purpose; a beast dies and (still) serves ten ends. What do I know of the course of my own deeds? What do I know, O Baba? The bones burn like a heap of wood; the hair burns like a bundle of grass. Says Kabir: man wakes up only then, when the rod of Jam strikes (his) head. ॥3॥
870.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. The Expanse (the all-pervading Lord) is in the heavens, the Expanse is in the underworld, the Expanse abides in all four directions; he is the source of bliss, ever the Supreme Being; the body perishes, (but) the Expanse does not pass away. Detachment has arisen in me: this soul came, and where has it gone? The five elements joined and made the body; (but) from where were the elements made? You call the soul bound by karma; (but) who put life into karma? The body is in the Lord, the Lord is in the body; he is within all, with no gap between. Says Kabir: I will not give up the Name of Ram; whatever comes of itself, let it come. ॥3॥
870.4: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Binding (my) arms, they threw (me) down like a clod (before the elephant); in anger, (the driver) struck the elephant on its head; (but) the elephant flees, crying out: I am a sacrifice to this form. O my Master, yours is the strength (I rely on); the Qazi is shouting: urge the elephant on! O driver, I will cut you to pieces; make it move, strike a blow. (But) the elephant does not move; it stands absorbed in meditation; the Lord dwells in its heart. What crime has the Sant committed, that (he) has been tied up in a bundle and given to the elephant? The elephant lifts the bundle again and again and bows to it; (but) the Qazi, in his darkness, did not understand. Three times he put it to the test; (yet his) hard heart was still not convinced. Says Kabir: Gobind is ours (to protect us); the life of the servant rests in the fourth state. ॥4॥
The fourth state (turiya): the spiritual state beyond Maya's three qualities.
871.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. It is neither a man nor a god; it is not known as a celibate, nor as a devotee of Shiva; it is neither a yogi nor an avadhut; it has no mother, nor is it anyone's son. Who is it that dwells in this temple (of the body)? no one finds the end of it. It is neither a householder nor a renunciant; it is neither a king nor does it beg for alms; it has no body, not a speck of blood; it is neither a Brahmin nor a Kshatriya. It is not known as an ascetic, nor as a Sheikh; it neither lives nor dies: see (this). If anyone weeps over it as dying, the one who weeps loses his own honour. By the Guru's grace I have found the path, and have had both living and dying erased. Says Kabir: this is a part of Ram, as ink upon paper is not erased. ॥4॥
871.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. The threads (of the warp) are broken, the sizing is used up; at the door the (idle) reeds glint; the poor brushes have fallen apart, bristle by bristle; death rides on the head of this shaven one. This shaven one is throwing away all (our) wealth; with (holy men) coming and going, (I) am harried to the point of death. (He) has given up all thought of the cloth-beam and the bobbin; his mind is dyed in the Name of Ram. There is nothing for the girls and boys to eat; (yet) the shaven ones leave well fed every day. One or two are in the house, one or two on the road; for us a mat on the floor, for them the bed; (they come) stroking (their shaven) heads, with books tied at the waist; for us parched grain to chew, for them bread. The shaven ones have become one with the shaven; these shaven ones are a prop for those who are drowning. Listen, Loi, blind and without a guide: hasten to the refuge of these shaven ones, (says) Kabir. ॥4॥

The first three stanzas are the household's complaint about Kabir; the fourth is Kabir's answer. By tradition, Loi was the name of Kabir's wife; mundia, the shaven one, is a holy man, a devotee of the Lord.
The warp, the sizing, the reeds, the brushes, the cloth-beam and the bobbin are a weaver's gear; Kabir was a weaver.
871.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. When the husband dies, the woman does not weep, for someone else becomes her keeper; (then) that keeper too perishes; hereafter (lies) hell, here pleasures and revels. One ever-wedded bride (Maya) is the darling of the world, the wife of all beings and creatures. A necklace adorns the bride's neck; to the Sant she is poison, (but) the world delights (in her). Decked in finery, she sits (like) a harlot; (but) cursed by the Sant, the wretched one wanders about. Running, she goes after the Sant, (but) by the Guru's grace she fears (his) blows. She is the support of the Saakat's body (and life); to me she appears a fearsome witch. I have come to know her secret well since the divine Guru became kind and met (me). Says Kabir: now she has been put out, and clings to the hem of the world. ॥4॥
872.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. O brother, he in whose house there is no splendour (of wealth): the travellers who come (to his door) go away hungry; there is no contentment within him; without the ever-wedded bride (Maya), blame falls on him. Blessed is the ever-wedded bride, most pure, (without whom) the minds of ascetics and of the greatest ascetics waver. (Yet) this bride is the miser's daughter; passing over (the Lord's) servants, she has lain with the world. Standing at the Saadh's door, (she pleads:) (I am) in your refuge; carry me across. This bride is exceedingly beautiful; the anklets on her feet tinkle and jingle. As long as there is breath (in a man), she keeps him company; once it is gone, she is up at once and away, barefoot. This bride has taken the three worlds; she has drawn into her charm (the readers of) the eighteen Puranas and (the pilgrims to) the places of pilgrimage; she has pierced Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh; great lords of the earth and kings she has run through. This bride has neither a near shore nor a far one; she is in league with the five Narads (the senses). (But) the pots of (my) five Narads have burst. Says Kabir: by the Guru's grace (I) am set free (of her). ॥5॥
Narad is a sage of the Puranas, held to delight in stirring up quarrels between gods and men.
872.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. As in a house (the roof) does not hold up (without) a beam, (so) how can anyone cross over without the Naam? As water is not held without a pitcher, so without the Saadh (a man) departs without release. Let me burn him who does not remember Ram, and stays engrossed, body and mind, in the field (of the body). As land is not sown without one to drive the plough, how are beads strung with no thread? how is a knot fastened with no knob? so without the Saadh one departs without release. As no child is born without mother and father, how are clothes washed with no water? how can there be a rider with no horse? (so) without the Saadh there is no (reaching the Lord's) court. As no turn of the dance is taken without music, (so) the Husband has cast off the unloved wife and spurned her. Says Kabir: do the one thing worth doing: having become Gurmukh, one does not die again. ॥4॥
872.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. The kootan is he who pounds (his own) mind; (whoever) pounds the mind escapes Jam. He who pounds and pounds the mind and puts it to the touchstone, that kootan attains liberation in full. O world, whom do you call a kootan? Every word holds (more than one) sense. The nachan, the dancer, is he who dances with the mind, finds no comfort in falsehood, and is absorbed in the True One, (and) keeps the beat before this mind; the keeper of this dancer's mind (is the Lord himself). The bajari, the man of the bazaar, is he who searches the bazaar (of his body), awakens the five defiled ones (the senses), (and) comes to know devotion to the Master of the nine (regions of the earth); such a man of the bazaar I hold to be great. The taskar, the thief, is he who bears no envy, (and), holding the senses in check, utters the Naam. Says Kabir: such are my marks; blessed is the divine Guru, most beautiful and wise. ॥4॥
Kootan (a pimp; also one who pounds), nachan, bajari and taskar are terms of abuse; Kabir gives each a new sense.
873.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji. Blessed is Gopal, blessed is the divine Guru; blessed is grain, at which the lotus of the hungry man's heart opens. Blessed are those Sants who have understood this; Saringpani (the Lord who holds the bow) will meet them. Grain comes from the Primal Being; one should repeat the Naam while tasting grain. One should repeat the Naam, and one should repeat (the worth of) grain too; with water, (grain) takes on a fine colour. The men who keep away from grain lose their (honour) in the three worlds. Those who give up grain and practise hypocrisy are neither wedded wives nor widows. Before the world they call themselves dudhadhari (living on milk alone), (but) in secret they eat up the whole cake (of rice and pulse). Without grain there are no good times; by giving up grain, Gopal is not found. Says Kabir: this I have come to know: blessed is grain, (by which) the mind is won over to the Master. ॥4॥
Anaad: ann-aad, grain (as the Rahao line says, ann).
873.2: Raag Gond, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. If one performs the Ashvamedh sacrifice, gives in alms (gold and the like) to his own weight, and bathes at Prayag, even so (these) do not come up to the Lord's praise and the Naam. O lazy mind, worship your own Ram. If one offers pinds at Gaya, dwells at Banaras on the Asi, recites the four Vedas by heart, keeps all the religious duties, holds the senses firm by the teaching of his guru, and lives by the six duties, (or reads) the dialogue of Shiva and Shakti: O mind, give up, give up all these (rites, which keep you) apart; remember, remember Gobind; worship (him), O Nama, and you will cross the ocean of the world. ॥4॥
Ashvamedh: the horse sacrifice of kings. Pinds: balls of rice offered for the departed, at the tirath of Gaya.

The six duties (khat karam) are a Brahmin's: to study and to teach, to perform sacrifice and to have it performed, to give alms and to receive them. The dialogue of Shiva and Shakti: by the Darpan, the Ramayana, said to have been told by Shiva to Parvati.
873.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. As the deer runs after the sound (of the hunter's drum) and gives up its life, but its mind does not leave that (sound), so do I gaze on Ram, just so; leaving Ram, I turn my mind nowhere else. As the fisherman watches the fish, (as) the goldsmith eyes the gold he is shaping, as the lustful man eyes another's wife, (as) the gambler watches the cowries as he throws them, (so) wherever I look, there is Ram; Nama ever meditates on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
873.4: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Carry me across, O Ram, carry me across. I, your servant, am ignorant and know nothing of swimming; O Father Bithal, give (me your) arm. By the wisdom the True Guru teaches, a man becomes a god in an instant; the medicine by which, born of man, one has won heaven: may I obtain that medicine. Where you have set Dhru and Narad, set me too, if only a little. Leaning on your Name, many of your servants have been delivered: this is Nama's own conviction. ॥2॥
Dhru: the child prince who, slighted by his stepmother, gave himself to devotion and was given an unmoving place as the Pole Star.
874.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. A restless anguish has come upon me, (as on) a cow left alone without her calf. As a fish writhes without water, so does poor Nama (writhe) without the Name of Ram. As the cow's calf, let loose, sucks at the udder and gulps the butter, (so) Namdev has found Narayan; on meeting the Guru, the Unseen (Lord) has been made known (to him). As (the lustful man) is drawn to another's wife for pleasure, so Nama loves Murari (the foe of the demon Mur). As (creatures) burn in the glaring sun, so does poor Nama (writhe) without the Name of Ram. ॥5॥
874.2: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. Calling on the Lord, Har Har, all doubts are erased; take the Lord's Name: (this is) the highest dharma. calling on the Lord, Har Har, (the mark of) caste and lineage is taken away; that Lord is the blind man's staff. Salutations to the Lord, salutations to the Lord; calling on the Lord, Har Har, there is no pain from Jam. The Lord took the life of Harnakas; he gave Ajaimal a place in Baikunth (heaven); teaching a parrot (the Name of Ram), Ganika was saved; that Lord is the apple of (my) eye. Calling on the Lord, Har Har, Putna was saved, the slayer of children, full of deceit; by Simran the daughter of Dropad (Dropati) was saved; and Gautam's virtuous wife, (turned to) stone, was set free. He who destroyed Keshi and Kans, and granted Kali (the serpent) his life: Nama humbly prays: such is the Lord, repeating whose Name, fear and misfortune are averted. ॥4॥

Harnakas (Harnakhash, Hiranyakashipu): the demon king of the Puranas who tormented his son Prahlad for his devotion to God; God, as the Man-Lion, slew him. Ajaimal (Ajamal): a fallen Brahmin, saved when at death he called his son Narayan. Ganika: a courtesan, saved by teaching a parrot to say Ram.

Putna: the nurse sent by Kans to kill the child Krishna; she came with poison on her breasts, but Krishna, as he suckled, drew out her life, and she too was saved. Dropati (Draupadi): in the Mahabharata, the wife of the Pandavas, whom Duhsasan sought to strip in the court of the Kauravas, but her cloth did not run out. Ahalya: the wife of the sage Gautam, turned to stone by his curse and, in the Ramayana, set free at the touch of Ram.
Kans, Krishna's uncle, and Keshi, his champion, were slain by Krishna. Kali: the serpent Kaliya, whom, in the Puranas, Krishna subdued in the Yamuna.
874.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. (The man who) runs after Bhairau, ghosts and Sitala is a donkey-rider, scattering dust. As for me, I will take the One, the all-pervading Lord; all other gods I will give away in exchange (for him). The man who meditates (on Shiva), chanting Shiv, Shiv, rides a bull (like Shiva) and beats the damru (drum). (He who) worships Maha Mai, the Great Mother, is born again, from a man, as a woman. (O Bhavani,) you are called the primal Bhavani, (but) when it comes to (granting) liberation, where do you hide? O friend, through the Guru's teaching, take firm hold of the Name of Ram; Nama humbly prays: so says the Gita (too). ॥5॥
Bhairau: one of the fearsome forms of Shiva. Sitala is smallpox, which people took to be the wrath of the goddess Sitala; her mount is the donkey. Bhavani: a name of the goddess (Parvati, Durga).
874.4: Raag Bilaval Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji. Today Nama has seen Bithal; O (Pandit), let me make (you,) the fool, understand. O Pandit, your Gayatri was grazing in a Lodha's field; (he) took a stick and broke (her) leg, and she went off limping, limping. O Pandit, your Mahadev was seen coming, riding a white bull; food was cooked (for him) in the house of the modi (the storekeeper), (yet he) killed that man's son. O Pandit, your Ram Chand too was seen coming; (he) went to war with Ravan, (for he) had lost his own wife. The Hindu is blind, the Turk is one-eyed; wiser than both is the one who knows (God). The Hindu worships the temple, the Muslim the mosque; Nama has served him (alone), where there is neither temple nor mosque. ॥4॥

The first three stanzas recall stories the Pandit himself tells of those he worships: by a curse the Gayatri was born a cow and grazed a Lodha's field (the Lodhas are a farming caste), and Mahadev (Shiva) by a curse killed the son of the modi at whose house his food was cooked.
875.1: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace. O world, repeat (the Name of) Mukand (the giver of liberation), Mukand; without Mukand the body wastes away for nothing. That Mukand is the giver of liberation; that Mukand is my father and mother. Living, (he dwells on) Mukand; dying, (on) Mukand: such a servant of his lives ever in bliss. Mukand, Mukand is (the stay of) my life; repeating Mukand, the mark (of good fortune shines) on my brow; the one detached from the world serves Mukand; I, the weak, have found that very Mukand as (my) wealth. If the One Mukand shows (me) kindness, what harm can the world do me? (he) has wiped out (my) caste, and (I) now belong to (his) court; O Mukand, you alone are able to carry (souls) across, age after age. Knowledge has sprung up (in me), and light has dawned; in his grace (the Lord) has taken (me), his servant, lowly as a worm, for his own. Says Ravidas: now (my) craving is at an end; I repeat (the Name of) Mukand, and serve him alone. ॥4॥
875.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji. Even if he (the slanderer) bathes at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage, even if he worships the twelve stones (of Shiva), even if he has wells and tanks dug, (yet if) he slanders (the Saadh), it all goes for nothing. How can the slanderer of the Saadh be saved? know for certain that he falls into hell. Even if he bathes at an eclipse at Kulkhet (Kurukshetra), gives away his wife in alms, with all her ornaments, (and) hears all the Simritis with his ears, (yet if) he slanders (the Saadh), none of it is of any use. Even if he has many feasts served, and, giving land in alms, wins renown in the world, (and) spoils his own (affairs) to set others' right, (yet if) he slanders (the Saadh), he roams through many births. O world, why do you slander? the slanderer's (false) shop is (soon) laid bare. Searching and testing, (I) have weighed (the end of) the slanderer: says Ravidas: (that) sinner has departed for hell.
Jor (the total): the closing figures 11, 7 and 2 are the counts of the shabads of Kabir, Namdev and Ravidas in Raag Gond, and 49 that of all the shabads of Raag Gond.

859.1: There is one God, Ik Oankar, the One who pervades all and is ever the same; his Name is Sat (the One who truly is); he is the Creator, the Being who dwells in all, without fear, without enmity, his form beyond time, unborn, self-existent, realised by the Guru's grace.
Raag Gond, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
If you keep your hope in the Lord, in your mind and heart, you will gain many, many fruits your mind desires;
the Lord knows all that passes within the soul; God lets not even a sesame seed's worth of anyone's labour go to waste.
O my mind, hope should be placed in that Lord, the Master who pervades all.
O my mind, set your hope on the Lord of the world, the earth's Master.
Any hope that is placed in anyone but the Lord is fruitless; that hope all goes in vain.
All the family you see is attachment to Maya (the world's illusion and lure); beware of wasting your life clinging to hope in it.
Nothing is in their hands; what can these poor ones do? Their striving avails nothing.
O my mind, place your hope in the Lord, your own Beloved, who carries you across and sets all your family free.
If you place any other hope, in Maya, do not imagine it will be of any use to you.
This hope in Maya is the love of another; it is false, and in an instant it all perishes.
O my mind, place your hope in the Lord, your true Beloved, who accepts all your labour.
All hope and desire are yours, my Master; as you make one hope, so does one hope.
Nothing is in anyone's hands, my Master; such is the understanding my True Guru has given me.
You know servant Nanak's hope; beholding the Lord's sight, he is fulfilled by the Lord's sight. ॥4॥
860.1: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
One should serve such a Lord, and meditate on him every day, who destroys all sins in an instant.
If one forsakes the Lord and places hope in another, the Lord makes all one's labour fruitless and lets it go to waste.
O my mind, serve the Lord, the Master, the giver of peace; serving him, all hunger departs.
O my mind, one should put one's trust in the Lord.
Wherever one goes, my Master is there alongside; the Lord keeps the honour of his servants and slaves as his own.
If you tell your pain to others, they in return lay out their own pain, ever so much more.
Tell your pain to the Lord, your own Master, who cuts away your sorrows at once.
Should one leave such a God and tell one's pain to others? Telling it to others, O mind, one dies of shame.
The family, friends and brothers of the world whom you see, O my mind, all meet (you) for their own ends.
On the day their purpose is not served, on that day not one comes near.
O my mind, serve your own Lord day and night, who helps you in sorrow and in joy.
Why should one trust, O my mind, one who cannot save (us) at the final hour?
Take the Guru's teaching and repeat the mantra of the Lord's Name; those with the Lord's love in their hearts are set free by him at the end.
Says servant Nanak, O Sants (saints) of the Lord, repeat the Naam (the Name, God's presence remembered) night and day; this is the true assurance of release. ॥4॥
860.2: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
Remembering the Lord, there is bliss and peace always, calm within, and one's own mind grows cool,
as when the sun of Maya blazes fiercely, and on seeing the Guru, the moon, all the burning passes away.
O my mind, night and day meditate on the Naam and repeat (the Name of) the Lord.
He protects you wherever you are, in every place; serve such a God, your own, for ever.
O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord, in whom are all treasures; through the Guru, search and find the jewel of the Lord.
Those who meditated on the Lord found the Lord, my Master; massage the feet of those servants of the Lord.
Recognise the Shabad (the Word) and receive the essence of Ram (the Lord); (one who does) becomes an exalted Sant, the greatest of the great.
The Lord himself has increased the glory of that servant; he is not lessened by anyone's lessening, not by a sesame seed, not by the least bit.
O my mind, the One from whom you receive comforts, meditate on him always, ever with joined palms.
O Lord, give servant Nanak one gift: may your feet, Lord, dwell ever in my heart. ॥4॥
861.1: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
All the rich, the emperors, the nobles, the chiefs and the headmen there are, are perishable; know that the love of another is false.
The Lord is imperishable, ever abiding, unmoving; worship him, O my mind, and you will be accepted.
O my mind, worship the Name of the Lord, (your) everlasting support.
One who attains the Lord's mansion through the Guru's words: no one else has strength as great as his.
All the wealthy, the high-born and the owners of land that you see, O my mind, will perish like the fleeting colour of the safflower.
O my mind, ever serve the Lord, the True One, the Niranjan (the One untouched by Maya), through whom you will win honour in the Lord's court.
Brahmin, Khatri, Shudra and Vaish: there are four varnas (castes) and four ashrams; whoever meditates on the Lord is foremost.
As the lowly castor plant dwells beside the sandalwood (and takes its fragrance), so joining the Sat Sangat (the company of the true), the fallen one is accepted.
Highest of all and purest of all is the one in whose heart God has come to dwell.
Servant Nanak washes the feet of that servant of the Lord who serves him, though he be of low caste. ॥4॥
861.2: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
The Lord is the Knower of hearts, at work in all; as the Lord makes one act, so one acts.
Serve such a Lord always, O my mind, who saves you from everything.
O my mind, repeat (the Name of) the Lord; the Lord should be recited every day.
No one but the Lord can kill or bring to life; then, O my mind, why should one fret?
The Lord, the Creator, has made this whole expanse, and has himself placed his own light within it.
The one Lord speaks, the one Lord makes (all) speak; the perfect Guru has made (me) see the one Lord.
The Lord is with (us) within and with (us) without; say, O mind, what should one hide from him?
One should serve the Lord without guile; then, O my mind, every comfort is gained.
The One in whose power is everything is the greatest of all; O my mind, he should be meditated on always.
O servant Nanak, that Lord is with you; meditate on the Lord always, and he will set you free. ॥4॥
861.3: Raag Gond, by the Fourth Guru (Guru Ram Das Ji).
My mind burns greatly for the sight of the Lord, like one who thirsts without water.
The love of the Lord has pierced my mind like an arrow.
The Lord God knows my suffering, the ache within my mind.
Whoever tells me any word of my Beloved Lord is my brother, my own dear brother.
Meet me, meet me, my friend, and tell (me) the virtues of my God, taking the steadying counsel of the True Guru.
O Lord, fulfil servant Nanak's hope; in the Lord's sight the body finds peace.
862.1: Raag Gond, Ghar 1, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
(God) is the doer of all, and the enjoyer of all.
It is the Creator who hears, the Creator who sees;
the unseen is the Creator, the seen is the Creator;
the Creator brings creation, the Creator brings dissolution;
the Creator pervades all, and the Creator stays untouched.
It is the Creator who speaks, the Creator who understands;
the Creator comes, and the Creator too goes;
the Creator is Nirgun, the Creator is Sargun;
O Nanak, by the Guru's grace (one gains) the eye that sees (him) alike in all. ॥2॥
862.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Like the fish and the monkey, you are caught and tangled up in the safflower (of fleeting Maya).
Every step you take and every breath you draw is counted; sing the Lord's praises, and only then will you be saved.
O mind, understand, and give up your waywardness.
You find no place (here) to dwell for yourself; why then do you go to another's (house)?
As the elephant is driven by the lure of lust, so you cling to your family.
As birds gather and then part again, (so is the family); become steady in the Sangat and meditate on the Lord, Har Har.
As the fish perishes through the taste of the tongue, so the fool, lured by greed, is robbed;
you have fallen into the power of the five enemies (lust, anger, greed, attachment and pride); fall at (the Lord's) refuge, and only so will you be freed.
Be merciful, O destroyer of the sorrows of the meek; all beings and creatures are yours.
May I receive this gift, to behold your sight for ever; come and meet Nanak, the servant of your servants. ॥4॥
862.3: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, Chaupade, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
The One who fashioned (you) and gave (you) soul and breath,
who in his kindness placed (his) light in the clay (of the body),
(who gave you) everything to use, and (who) feeds you foods to enjoy:
forsaking that God, O fool, where do you go?
Let me devote myself to the service of the Supreme Lord.
It is through the Guru that the Niranjan, the divine Lord, is known.
The One who has made colours of many kinds,
(who brings about) creation and dissolution in the twinkling of an eye,
whose state and extent cannot be told:
O my mind, meditate on that God for ever.
The Master neither comes nor goes; he is unmoving.
His virtues are endless; how many can I count?
The One whose storehouses are full of the rubies of the Name
gives support to every heart.
The One whose Name is Sat Purakh (the True Being who pervades all):
millions of sins are erased: sing his praise for even an instant.
He is the companion from childhood, the friend of the devotees,
the support of the breath of life, the love of Nanak's heart. ॥4॥
863.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I have done my trading with the Naam;
the Naam alone is the support of this mind;
in my heart I have taken the Naam alone as my shelter;
repeating the Naam, millions of sins are erased.
As (my) capital, the Lord has given (me) the one Naam;
(the Naam) is my mind's beloved object of worship; in the Guru's company (my) attention dwells (on it).
The Naam is the capital of my soul;
wherever I go, the Naam alone is my companion;
the Naam alone has become sweet to my mind;
in water, on land, in all, I have seen the Naam alone.
Through the Naam, faces are radiant in the Lord's court;
through the Naam, all one's generations have been saved;
by the Naam my affairs have been accomplished;
this mind has grown fond of the Naam.
Through the Naam alone I have grown fearless;
through the Naam, (my) coming and going (in births) has ended;
the perfect Guru has brought (me) to the Treasure of virtues.
Says Nanak, (my) dwelling is (now) in peace and in Sahaj (natural, unshaken poise). ॥4॥
863.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The One who gives honour to the dishonoured,
who gives his gifts to all the hungry,
who protects (us) in the dreadful womb:
to that Master be salutation for ever.
Meditate in your mind on such a God,
the helper in easy places and in hard, wherever one may be.
To whom the pauper and the king are alike,
who fills all, the worm and the elephant,
who asks no second one and takes no one's counsel:
whatever he does, he does himself.
Whose end no one can know:
he, the Niranjan, is all himself;
he himself is form, he himself is formless;
(he dwells) in every heart, the support of all hearts.
In the dye of the Naam, the devotees have become deep red;
singing (his) praise, the Sants are ever in delight;
in the love of the Naam, (his) servants remain fulfilled;
Nanak falls at the feet of those servants. ॥4॥
863.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Those in whose company this mind (becomes) pure,
in whose company there is Simran (remembrance) of the Lord, Har Har,
in whose company sins are destroyed,
in whose company the heart is filled with light:
those Sants of the Lord are my friends,
in whose presence the Naam alone is sung every day.
By whose mantra the Lord, Har Har, comes to dwell in the mind,
by whose teaching doubt and fear flee,
in whose presence is (the Lord's) pure and sublime praise,
whose dust (of the feet) the world longs for;
in whose company millions of the fallen are saved,
whose support is the Name of the one Formless Lord,
(who) knows the hidden heart of every being,
the treasure of mercy, the Niranjan, the divine Lord.
When the Supreme Lord became merciful,
then (I) met the Guru, the merciful Saadh (the holy one).
Nanak meditates on the Naam day and night;
through the Lord's Name come peace, Sahaj and bliss. ॥4॥
864.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In my mind I meditate on the form of the Guru;
through the Guru's Shabad, my mind holds to the mantra (of the Name);
I take the Guru's feet and enshrine them in my heart;
to the Guru, the Supreme Lord, I bow for ever.
Let no one in the world be misled by doubt:
without the Guru no one will cross over.
The Guru has set the strayed upon the path;
having (him) give up all else, he has joined him to the Lord's devotion;
he has erased the dread of birth and death.
Boundless is the greatness of the perfect Guru.
By the Guru's grace, the inverted lotus (of the heart) blossoms;
in the darkness, light has dawned;
the One who made (us) has been known through the Guru;
by the Guru's grace the foolish mind has been won over.
The Guru is the Creator; the Guru has power to do all;
the Guru is the Supreme God, who is and also shall be.
Says Nanak, God has made this known (to me):
without the Guru, O brother, liberation is not attained. ॥4॥
864.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Say Guru, Guru, Guru, O my mind.
Without the Guru I have no other.
Stay in the Guru's support day and night,
whose gift no one can erase.
Know the Guru and the Supreme God as one;
what pleases him is accepted.
The one whose mind is fixed on the Guru's feet:
his sorrow, pain and doubt run away.
Serving the Guru, one gains honour;
(I am) ever a sacrifice to the Guru.
Beholding the Guru's sight, (the mind) is filled with delight;
the labour of the Guru's servant comes to fruition;
no sorrow afflicts the Guru's servant;
the Guru's servant is known in all ten directions.
The Guru's greatness is beyond telling;
the Guru, the Supreme Lord, pervades (all).
Says Nanak, the one whose destiny is perfect
has his mind fixed on the Guru's feet. ॥4॥
864.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Guru is my worship; the Guru is Gobind (the Lord of the universe);
my Guru is Paarbrahm (the Supreme Lord); the Guru is God;
my Guru is the divine Lord, unseen and beyond knowing;
I serve the Guru's feet, which all worship.
Without the Guru there is no other place for me;
night and day I repeat the name of the Guru, the Guru.
The Guru is my wisdom; the Guru is the meditation in my heart;
the Guru is Gopal (the Lord who sustains all), the all-pervading Being, God;
with joined palms I remain in the Guru's refuge;
without the Guru I have no other.
The Guru is the ship that carries (us) across the ocean of the world;
through the Guru's service comes release from Jam (the messenger of Death);
the Guru's mantra is light amid the darkness;
in the Guru's company, all are delivered.
It is by great good fortune that the perfect Guru is found;
serving the Guru, sorrow does not touch (one);
no one can erase the Guru's Shabad;
the Guru is Nanak, and Nanak is that Lord himself. ॥4॥
865.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Do your trading with (the Name of) Ram, Ram;
(make) Ram, Ram, Ram the support of your breath of life;
sing the Kirtan (songs of God's praise) of Ram, Ram, Ram;
the all-pervading Ram is contained in all.
Join the Sants and utter (the Name of) Ram:
(this) is the purest of all deeds, one that is complete.
Gather the wealth of Ram, Ram, and fill (your) storehouse;
make Ram, Ram, Ram your food;
may (the Name of) Ram, Ram never be forgotten:
the Guru, in his mercy, has told (me this).
Ram, Ram, Ram is ever the helper;
fix your attention in love on Ram, Ram, Ram;
repeating Ram, Ram, (they) have become pure,
and the sins of birth after birth have gone.
Remembering Ram, (he) ends birth and death;
uttering Ram, (he) carries (one) across (the ocean of) fear.
Ram, the radiant One, is highest of all;
O servant Nanak, repeat (his Name) night and day. ॥4॥
865.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Master held them (the five) in check, and they were beaten;
he beat them and drove them away from (his) servant.
They could not find the mansion of Gobind's devotee;
the servants of Ram have joined together and sung songs of joy.
The five chiefs of all creation (the five enemies)
are water-carriers to the devotee of Ram.
They take tribute from the world,
but bow in salute to Gobind's devotee;
they plunder the Saakats (those who have turned from God) and strip them of honour,
but they rub and wash the feet of the holy.
One mother (Maya) has borne five sons;
making the play of the earth-born (and the other sources of life), she has given birth to the world.
(Beings) revel, absorbed in the three qualities (of Maya);
leaving these behind, (the Lord's) servants dwell above.
In his mercy (the Lord) has set his servants free;
the One whose (servants) they are has kept (the five) away from them.
Says Nanak, devotion to God is the essence;
without devotion, all are ruined. ॥4॥
865.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Through the Lord's Name, strife and anguish have been erased;
sorrows have been destroyed, and peace has made its home (within);
repeating again and again the Naam, the Amrit (the nectar that gives spiritual life), (his servants) are fulfilled;
by the Sant's grace (they) have obtained every fruit.
Repeating Ram, (his) servants have crossed over;
the sins of birth after birth have been taken away.
Those who have enshrined the Guru's feet in the heart, within the breast,
have crossed over the ocean of fire;
all the torment of birth and death is erased;
in Sahaj, (they) are absorbed in God.
In every place and space is the one Master;
he is the Knower of all hearts;
the one to whom, in his mercy, he gives understanding
takes God's Name at all hours.
The one within whom God himself dwells:
in his heart there is light.
With loving devotion, one should sing the Lord's Kirtan;
O Nanak, repeating (the Name of) the Supreme Lord, one is carried across. ॥4॥
865.4: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Bow to the lotus feet of the Guru;
slay lust and anger, (driving them) out of this body;
one should live as the dust (of the feet) of all;
recognise the all-pervading Lord in every heart, in all.
In this way remember Gopal, Gobind:
the body and wealth are God's, and the soul is God's.
Sing the Lord's praises at all hours;
this is the purpose of soul and breath;
give up pride and know God to be with (you);
by the Saadh's grace, dye your mind in the Lord('s love).
Know the One who made you;
(such a one) wins honour hereafter in the Lord's court;
(his) mind and body become pure and filled with delight,
as the tongue repeats the Name of Gopal.
Show mercy, my (Lord), merciful to the meek:
(my) mind asks for the dust under the Saadh's feet.
Be kind, O God, and give (this) gift:
that Nanak may live by repeating God's Name. ॥4॥
866.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Service of Gopal is (my) incense and lamp;
to the Creator (I) bow countless times.
Leaving all else, (I) have taken hold of God's refuge;
by great good fortune, the Guru is greatly pleased (with me).
At all hours one should sing of Gobind;
the body and wealth are God's, and the soul is God's.
Uttering the Lord's virtues, joy has come;
the Supreme Lord is all-pervading, the one who forgives.
In his mercy he joins his servants to his service,
erases (their) pain of birth and death, and unites (them with himself).
This is the (true) deed, this the dharma, this the essence of wisdom:
in the Saadh Sangat (the company of the holy) one should repeat the Lord's Name.
Cross the (world-)ocean on the ship of the feet of God,
who knows every heart and does and causes all to be done.
Bestowing his mercy, (God) has kept (his own) safe;
the five dreadful enemies have fled.
(The Lord's servant) never loses (his) life in the gamble;
the Creator has taken Nanak's side. ॥4॥
866.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
In his mercy (God) grants peace and bliss;
the divine Guru has kept (his) children safe.
God, Gobind, is kind and merciful,
the forgiver of all beings and creatures.
(I have come to) your refuge, God, merciful to the meek;
repeating (the Name of) the Supreme Lord, one is ever in delight.
O God, there is none other so merciful;
you are within every heart, contained in all.
(God) sets right this world and the next for his servant;
to purify the fallen, O God, is your age-old way.
Remember Gobind: (this is) millions of medicines;
one should worship the Lord: (this is) the tantra and the mantra.
Meditating on God, illness and grief are wiped away,
and one gains in full the fruits the mind desires.
(God) does and causes all to be done; he is all-powerful and merciful;
in deep reflection on him lie all treasures.
O Nanak, God himself has forgiven (his servants);
for ever and ever repeat (the Name of) the one Lord. ॥4॥
866.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Repeat the Name of the Lord, Har Har, my friend;
your mind will become pure.
Every affliction of mind and body is erased,
and all pain and darkness depart.
Singing the Lord's praises, one crosses the world (-ocean);
by great good fortune, the infinite Being is found.
The one who sings the Kirtan of Gopal
cannot be touched by Jamkaal (death).
His coming into the world is approved;
through the Guru, recognise your own Master.
(The one who) sings the Lord's praises by the Sant's grace:
(his) frenzies of lust and anger are erased.
Know the Lord to be ever present;
(this is) the perfect Guru's flawless mantra.
(One who) has earned the wealth of the Lord and filled (his) storehouses
has, meeting the True Guru, set all (his) affairs right;
(he) has woken up, dyed in the Lord's Name;
O Nanak, (his) mind clings to the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
867.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The Lord's feet are the ship across the world-ocean;
remembering the Naam, there is no dying again.
Uttering the Lord's praises, one does not walk the road of Jam;
deep reflection (on God) crushes the five enemies.
I have come to your refuge, O perfect Master;
give your hand to your own creature.
The Simritis, the Shastras, the Vedas and the Puranas
expound the Supreme Lord;
yogis, celibates, Vaishnavs and servants of Ram (tell of him too),
(yet) God, the Imperishable, has no measure.
Shiva and the gods cry out in entreaty,
(but) they grasp not a sesame seed's worth of the unseen, unfathomable (Lord).
Whoever is given loving devotion by (God) himself:
such are rare in the world, only one here and there.
In me, who am without virtue, there is no virtue at all;
in your glance (of grace) are all the treasures.
Nanak, the meek, begs for your service;
be merciful, O divine Guru, and grant (it). ॥4॥
867.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
(God says:) the one cursed by the Sant I tear out from the earth;
the Sant's slanderer I hurl down from the sky.
The Sant I keep close to my own soul;
the Sant I save at once, in the time of a hand-clap.
He alone is a Sant who is pleasing to Ram;
the Sant and Gobind have but one work.
God places (his) hand over the Sant,
and dwells with the Sant day and night.
Breath by breath he sustains the Sants;
the Sant's foe he casts down from (his) throne.
Let no one slander the Sant;
whoever slanders comes to ruin.
The one whom the Creator protects:
let the whole world strive in vain (against him).
Trust in one's own God has come;
soul and body are all his capital.
This conviction has arisen in Nanak:
the manmukh (the self-willed) loses, and the Gurmukh (one who follows the Guru) ever wins. ॥4॥
867.3: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Water (your heart) with the immaculate Name of Narayan;
remembering it with the tongue, sins melt away.
Narayan dwells in all;
Narayan shines forth in every heart.
Those who utter (the Name of) Narayan do not go to hell;
serving Narayan, they obtain all fruits.
Narayan is the support within the mind;
Narayan is the ship across the world (-ocean).
Uttering (the Name of) Narayan, Jam turns and flees;
Narayan has broken the teeth of the witch (Maya).
Narayan is for ever and ever the forgiver;
Narayan has brought peace and bliss;
Narayan has made (his) glory manifest;
Narayan is the mother and father of the Sant.
In the Saadh Sangat it is Narayan, Narayan;
again and again Narayan is sung.
Meeting the Guru, (I) have found the thing beyond the reach of the senses;
servant Nanak has taken hold of Narayan's shelter. ॥4॥
868.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
The one whom the Protector protects:
the Formless Lord takes his side.
In the mother's womb, fire does not afflict him;
lust, anger, greed and attachment cannot touch him;
in the Saadh Sangat he repeats (the Name of) the Formless Lord;
ashes fall on the face of (his) slanderer.
(The Name of) Ram is the servant's shield and coat of mail;
the wicked foes cannot touch him.
Whoever takes pride (in himself) is undone;
the humble servant's refuge is God (himself).
Whoever has entered the refuge of the Lord, the King:
that servant (God) has kept safe, clasped to his bosom.
If anyone is very proud,
in an instant he is mingled with the dust.
The True One is now, and shall ever be;
I am a sacrifice (to him) for ever and ever.
Showing mercy, he has kept his servants safe;
Nanak's God is the support of the breath of life. ॥4॥
868.2: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Wondrous is the account, utterly beyond compare:
the soul is the form of the Supreme Lord.
It is neither old nor a child;
it has no pain, nor the net of Jam;
it neither perishes nor is born;
from the beginning, from the start of the ages, it has pervaded (all).
It feels no heat, it feels no cold;
it has no enemy, it has no friend;
it knows no elation, it knows no grief;
all things are its own; it has the power to do (all).
It has no father, it has no mother;
it lies past the farthest beyond, and has existed from the first.
The stain of sin and of virtue does not cling to it;
within every heart it is ever awake.
(God) created the one Shakti (Maya), with its three qualities;
this great Maya is his shadow.
He cannot be deceived or pierced, his secret cannot be known; he is merciful,
merciful to the meek, ever kind.
Of his state and extent nothing at all can be found;
Nanak goes as a sacrifice to him, again and again. ॥4॥
869.1: Raag Gond, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
I am a sacrifice to the Sants;
in the company of the Sants (I) sing the praises of Ram.
By the Sants' grace all sins are gone;
those of great fortune enter the Sants' refuge.
Repeating (the Name of) Ram, no obstacle takes hold;
by the Guru's grace one's own God is made known.
When the Supreme Lord becomes merciful,
he turns (one) into dust at the feet of the holy;
lust and anger leave this body,
and the jewel of Ram comes to dwell in the mind.
Fruitful and approved is the birth of that one (who knows God to be near):
know the Supreme Lord to be near at hand.
With loving devotion he is absorbed in God's Kirtan,
and, asleep for birth after birth, he awakens.
(God's) lotus feet are his servant's support;
I utter the praises of Govind: (this is) the true trade.
(O God,) fulfil the longing of (your) servants:
may Nanak find peace in the dust of (your) servants. ॥4॥
869.2: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, Ashtapadis, by the Fifth Guru (Guru Arjan Dev Ji).
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Bow to the perfect divine Guru,
whose very form bears fruit, whose service bears fruit;
(he is) the knower of hearts, the all-pervading Being, the Creator;
at all hours (he is) dyed in the love of the Naam.
The Guru is Gobind, the Guru is Gopal,
the protector of his own servant.
(The Guru) has won over emperors, kings and nobles;
he has struck down and destroyed the wicked and the proud;
he has put disease into the slanderer's mouth;
all the world hails (his) victory.
In the minds of the Sants is great bliss;
the Sants repeat (the Name of) the divine Guru, the Lord.
The faces of the Sangat have grown radiant;
the slanderer has lost every place (to stand).
With every breath the servant ever praises
the Supreme Lord, the Guru free of all want,
in whose refuge all fears are erased;
(he) has struck all slanderers down to the ground.
Let no one slander the servant (of the Lord);
whoever does comes to grief.
At all hours the servant meditates on the One;
Jam does not go near him.
The servants are without enmity, the slanderers are proud;
the servants wish (all) well, the slanderers are given to vice.
The Guru's Sikh has meditated on the True Guru;
the servants are saved; the slanderer has been cast into hell.
Listen, my friend, my dear companion:
at the Lord's door true words hold good:
as one does, so one receives;
the proud one's root is surely torn out.
O True Guru, the unsupported have you alone to lean on;
be merciful and keep (the honour) of your servant.
Says Nanak, I am a sacrifice to that Guru,
remembering whom (my) honour has been upheld. ॥8॥
870.1: Raag Gond, the hymns of the Bhagats: Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
When one meets a Sant, one should listen a little and speak a little;
when one meets one who is no Sant, one should keep silent.
O Baba, what kind of speech should one speak,
by which one may stay absorbed in the Name of Ram?
Speaking with the Sants does good;
speaking with a fool is labour in vain.
Talking on and on, the vices grow;
(yet) without speaking, what reflection can (people) make?
Says Kabir: the empty pitcher makes a sound;
the one that is full never wavers. ॥4॥
870.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
