When a man dies, the man serves no purpose;
a beast dies and (still) serves ten ends.
What do I know of the course of my own deeds?
What do I know, O Baba?
The bones burn like a heap of wood;
the hair burns like a bundle of grass.
Says Kabir: man wakes up only then,
when the rod of Jam strikes (his) head. ॥3॥
870.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The Expanse (the all-pervading Lord) is in the heavens, the Expanse is in the underworld, the Expanse abides in all four directions;
he is the source of bliss, ever the Supreme Being; the body perishes, (but) the Expanse does not pass away.
this soul came, and where has it gone?
The five elements joined and made the body; (but) from where were the elements made?
You call the soul bound by karma; (but) who put life into karma?
The body is in the Lord, the Lord is in the body; he is within all, with no gap between.
Says Kabir: I will not give up the Name of Ram; whatever comes of itself, let it come. ॥3॥
870.4: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Binding (my) arms, they threw (me) down like a clod (before the elephant);
in anger, (the driver) struck the elephant on its head;
(but) the elephant flees, crying out:
I am a sacrifice to this form.
O my Master, yours is the strength (I rely on);
the Qazi is shouting: urge the elephant on!
O driver, I will cut you to pieces;
make it move, strike a blow.
(But) the elephant does not move; it stands absorbed in meditation;
the Lord dwells in its heart.
What crime has the Sant committed,
that (he) has been tied up in a bundle and given to the elephant?
The elephant lifts the bundle again and again and bows to it;
(but) the Qazi, in his darkness, did not understand.
Three times he put it to the test;
(yet his) hard heart was still not convinced.
Says Kabir: Gobind is ours (to protect us);
the life of the servant rests in the fourth state. ॥4॥
871.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
It is neither a man nor a god;
it is not known as a celibate, nor as a devotee of Shiva;
it is neither a yogi nor an avadhut;
it has no mother, nor is it anyone's son.
Who is it that dwells in this temple (of the body)?
no one finds the end of it.
It is neither a householder nor a renunciant;
it is neither a king nor does it beg for alms;
it has no body, not a speck of blood;
it is neither a Brahmin nor a Kshatriya.
It is not known as an ascetic, nor as a Sheikh;
it neither lives nor dies: see (this).
If anyone weeps over it as dying,
the one who weeps loses his own honour.
By the Guru's grace I have found the path,
and have had both living and dying erased.
Says Kabir: this is a part of Ram,
as ink upon paper is not erased. ॥4॥
871.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The threads (of the warp) are broken, the sizing is used up;
at the door the (idle) reeds glint;
the poor brushes have fallen apart, bristle by bristle;
death rides on the head of this shaven one.
This shaven one is throwing away all (our) wealth;
with (holy men) coming and going, (I) am harried to the point of death.
(He) has given up all thought of the cloth-beam and the bobbin;
his mind is dyed in the Name of Ram.
There is nothing for the girls and boys to eat;
(yet) the shaven ones leave well fed every day.
One or two are in the house, one or two on the road;
for us a mat on the floor, for them the bed;
(they come) stroking (their shaven) heads, with books tied at the waist;
for us parched grain to chew, for them bread.
The shaven ones have become one with the shaven;
these shaven ones are a prop for those who are drowning.
Listen, Loi, blind and without a guide:
hasten to the refuge of these shaven ones, (says) Kabir. ॥4॥
871.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
When the husband dies, the woman does not weep,
for someone else becomes her keeper;
(then) that keeper too perishes;
hereafter (lies) hell, here pleasures and revels.
One ever-wedded bride (Maya) is the darling of the world,
the wife of all beings and creatures.
A necklace adorns the bride's neck;
to the Sant she is poison, (but) the world delights (in her).
Decked in finery, she sits (like) a harlot;
(but) cursed by the Sant, the wretched one wanders about.
Running, she goes after the Sant,
(but) by the Guru's grace she fears (his) blows.
She is the support of the Saakat's body (and life);
to me she appears a fearsome witch.
I have come to know her secret well
since the divine Guru became kind and met (me).
Says Kabir: now she has been put out,
and clings to the hem of the world. ॥4॥
872.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
O brother, he in whose house there is no splendour (of wealth):
the travellers who come (to his door) go away hungry;
there is no contentment within him;
without the ever-wedded bride (Maya), blame falls on him.
Blessed is the ever-wedded bride, most pure,
(without whom) the minds of ascetics and of the greatest ascetics waver.
(Yet) this bride is the miser's daughter;
passing over (the Lord's) servants, she has lain with the world.
Standing at the Saadh's door, (she pleads:)
(I am) in your refuge; carry me across.
This bride is exceedingly beautiful;
the anklets on her feet tinkle and jingle.
As long as there is breath (in a man), she keeps him company;
once it is gone, she is up at once and away, barefoot.
This bride has taken the three worlds;
she has drawn into her charm (the readers of) the eighteen Puranas and (the pilgrims to) the places of pilgrimage;
she has pierced Brahma, Vishnu and Mahesh;
great lords of the earth and kings she has run through.
This bride has neither a near shore nor a far one;
she is in league with the five Narads (the senses).
(But) the pots of (my) five Narads have burst.
Says Kabir: by the Guru's grace (I) am set free (of her). ॥5॥
872.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
As in a house (the roof) does not hold up (without) a beam,
(so) how can anyone cross over without the Naam?
As water is not held without a pitcher,
so without the Saadh (a man) departs without release.
Let me burn him who does not remember Ram,
and stays engrossed, body and mind, in the field (of the body).
As land is not sown without one to drive the plough,
how are beads strung with no thread?
how is a knot fastened with no knob?
so without the Saadh one departs without release.
As no child is born without mother and father,
how are clothes washed with no water?
how can there be a rider with no horse?
(so) without the Saadh there is no (reaching the Lord's) court.
As no turn of the dance is taken without music,
(so) the Husband has cast off the unloved wife and spurned her.
Says Kabir: do the one thing worth doing:
having become Gurmukh, one does not die again. ॥4॥
872.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
The kootan is he who pounds (his own) mind;
(whoever) pounds the mind escapes Jam.
He who pounds and pounds the mind and puts it to the touchstone,
that kootan attains liberation in full.
O world, whom do you call a kootan?
Every word holds (more than one) sense.
The nachan, the dancer, is he who dances with the mind,
finds no comfort in falsehood, and is absorbed in the True One,
(and) keeps the beat before this mind;
the keeper of this dancer's mind (is the Lord himself).
The bajari, the man of the bazaar, is he who searches the bazaar (of his body),
awakens the five defiled ones (the senses),
(and) comes to know devotion to the Master of the nine (regions of the earth);
such a man of the bazaar I hold to be great.
The taskar, the thief, is he who bears no envy,
(and), holding the senses in check, utters the Naam.
Says Kabir: such are my marks;
blessed is the divine Guru, most beautiful and wise. ॥4॥
873.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Kabir Ji.
Blessed is Gopal, blessed is the divine Guru;
blessed is grain, at which the lotus of the hungry man's heart opens.
Blessed are those Sants who have understood this;
Saringpani (the Lord who holds the bow) will meet them.
Grain comes from the Primal Being;
one should repeat the Naam while tasting grain.
One should repeat the Naam, and one should repeat (the worth of) grain too;
with water, (grain) takes on a fine colour.
The men who keep away from grain
lose their (honour) in the three worlds.
Those who give up grain and practise hypocrisy
are neither wedded wives nor widows.
Before the world they call themselves dudhadhari (living on milk alone),
(but) in secret they eat up the whole cake (of rice and pulse).
Without grain there are no good times;
by giving up grain, Gopal is not found.
Says Kabir: this I have come to know:
blessed is grain, (by which) the mind is won over to the Master. ॥4॥
873.2: Raag Gond, Ghar 1, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
If one performs the Ashvamedh sacrifice,
gives in alms (gold and the like) to his own weight,
and bathes at Prayag,
even so (these) do not come up to the Lord's praise and the Naam.
O lazy mind, worship your own Ram.
If one offers pinds at Gaya,
dwells at Banaras on the Asi,
recites the four Vedas by heart,
keeps all the religious duties,
holds the senses firm by the teaching of his guru,
and lives by the six duties,
(or reads) the dialogue of Shiva and Shakti:
O mind, give up, give up all these (rites, which keep you) apart;
remember, remember Gobind;
worship (him), O Nama, and you will cross the ocean of the world. ॥4॥
873.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
As the deer runs after the sound (of the hunter's drum)
and gives up its life, but its mind does not leave that (sound),
so do I gaze on Ram, just so;
leaving Ram, I turn my mind nowhere else.
As the fisherman watches the fish,
(as) the goldsmith eyes the gold he is shaping,
as the lustful man eyes another's wife,
(as) the gambler watches the cowries as he throws them,
(so) wherever I look, there is Ram;
Nama ever meditates on the Lord's feet. ॥4॥
873.4: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Carry me across, O Ram, carry me across.
I, your servant, am ignorant and know nothing of swimming; O Father Bithal, give (me your) arm.
By the wisdom the True Guru teaches, a man becomes a god in an instant;
the medicine by which, born of man, one has won heaven: may I obtain that medicine.
Where you have set Dhru and Narad, set me too, if only a little.
Leaning on your Name, many of your servants have been delivered: this is Nama's own conviction. ॥2॥
874.1: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
A restless anguish has come upon me,
(as on) a cow left alone without her calf.
As a fish writhes without water,
so does poor Nama (writhe) without the Name of Ram.
As the cow's calf, let loose,
sucks at the udder and gulps the butter,
on meeting the Guru, the Unseen (Lord) has been made known (to him).
As (the lustful man) is drawn to another's wife for pleasure,
so Nama loves Murari (the foe of the demon Mur).
As (creatures) burn in the glaring sun,
so does poor Nama (writhe) without the Name of Ram. ॥5॥
874.2: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
Calling on the Lord, Har Har, all doubts are erased;
take the Lord's Name: (this is) the highest dharma.
calling on the Lord, Har Har, (the mark of) caste and lineage is taken away;
that Lord is the blind man's staff.
Salutations to the Lord, salutations to the Lord;
calling on the Lord, Har Har, there is no pain from Jam.
The Lord took the life of Harnakas;
he gave Ajaimal a place in Baikunth (heaven);
teaching a parrot (the Name of Ram), Ganika was saved;
that Lord is the apple of (my) eye.
Calling on the Lord, Har Har, Putna was saved,
the slayer of children, full of deceit;
by Simran the daughter of Dropad (Dropati) was saved;
and Gautam's virtuous wife, (turned to) stone, was set free.
He who destroyed Keshi and Kans,
and granted Kali (the serpent) his life:
Nama humbly prays: such is the Lord,
repeating whose Name, fear and misfortune are averted. ॥4॥
874.3: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
(The man who) runs after Bhairau, ghosts and Sitala
As for me, I will take the One, the all-pervading Lord;
all other gods I will give away in exchange (for him).
The man who meditates (on Shiva), chanting Shiv, Shiv,
rides a bull (like Shiva) and beats the damru (drum).
(He who) worships Maha Mai, the Great Mother,
is born again, from a man, as a woman.
(O Bhavani,) you are called the primal Bhavani,
(but) when it comes to (granting) liberation, where do you hide?
O friend, through the Guru's teaching, take firm hold of the Name of Ram;
Nama humbly prays: so says the Gita (too). ॥5॥
874.4: Raag Bilaval Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Namdev Ji.
Today Nama has seen Bithal; O (Pandit), let me make (you,) the fool, understand.
O Pandit, your Gayatri was grazing in a Lodha's field;
(he) took a stick and broke (her) leg, and she went off limping, limping.
O Pandit, your Mahadev was seen coming, riding a white bull;
food was cooked (for him) in the house of the modi (the storekeeper), (yet he) killed that man's son.
O Pandit, your Ram Chand too was seen coming;
(he) went to war with Ravan, (for he) had lost his own wife.
The Hindu is blind, the Turk is one-eyed;
wiser than both is the one who knows (God).
The Hindu worships the temple, the Muslim the mosque;
Nama has served him (alone), where there is neither temple nor mosque. ॥4॥
875.1: Raag Gond, Ghar 2, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Ik Oankar: God is One, the all-pervading Creator, realised through the True Guru's grace.
O world, repeat (the Name of) Mukand (the giver of liberation), Mukand;
without Mukand the body wastes away for nothing.
That Mukand is the giver of liberation;
that Mukand is my father and mother.
Living, (he dwells on) Mukand; dying, (on) Mukand:
such a servant of his lives ever in bliss.
Mukand, Mukand is (the stay of) my life;
repeating Mukand, the mark (of good fortune shines) on my brow;
the one detached from the world serves Mukand;
I, the weak, have found that very Mukand as (my) wealth.
If the One Mukand shows (me) kindness,
what harm can the world do me?
(he) has wiped out (my) caste, and (I) now belong to (his) court;
O Mukand, you alone are able to carry (souls) across, age after age.
Knowledge has sprung up (in me), and light has dawned;
in his grace (the Lord) has taken (me), his servant, lowly as a worm, for his own.
Says Ravidas: now (my) craving is at an end;
I repeat (the Name of) Mukand, and serve him alone. ॥4॥
875.2: Raag Gond, the hymn of Bhagat Ravidas Ji.
Even if he (the slanderer) bathes at the sixty-eight places of pilgrimage,
even if he worships the twelve stones (of Shiva),
even if he has wells and tanks dug,
(yet if) he slanders (the Saadh), it all goes for nothing.
How can the slanderer of the Saadh be saved?
know for certain that he falls into hell.
Even if he bathes at an eclipse at Kulkhet (Kurukshetra),
gives away his wife in alms, with all her ornaments,
(and) hears all the Simritis with his ears,
(yet if) he slanders (the Saadh), none of it is of any use.
Even if he has many feasts served,
and, giving land in alms, wins renown in the world,
(and) spoils his own (affairs) to set others' right,
(yet if) he slanders (the Saadh), he roams through many births.
O world, why do you slander?
the slanderer's (false) shop is (soon) laid bare.
Searching and testing, (I) have weighed (the end of) the slanderer:
says Ravidas: (that) sinner has departed for hell.
